coverage.evidence: The states each screen's spec declares are all present and unchanged in number: Quick Add has its empty, invalid, saving and rejected states, and Plan has its no-categories and nothing-allocated empty states. What this change alters is only when Quick Add's state is created, and the eight tests covering those states pass. The spec is docs/06-page-specs.md section 7.5 for Quick Add and 7.3 for Plan; neither's behaviour prose is touched, so the design-data contract is not engaged.

coverage.reason: Offline is unchanged: no network call, service worker or cache is in scope.

coverage.evidence: No design value is written directly by any changed line. app-shell's addition is an integer counter and a function; quick-add loses an effect; plan-screen loses a memo. No colour, spacing, radius or font size appears in the diff at all, and the classes around them are token classes — min-h-target, px-16, text-body, bg-card.
Tokens still come from one place: apps/web/src/design/tokens.css declares both palettes and tailwind.config.ts reads them through var(). Nothing in this change adds a second source or a literal.

coverage.reason: No token is added or renamed. The existing names in scope are purposeful rather than visual — ink, soft, card, line, target-min, em2.

coverage.evidence: Both screens are still built from the shared set — Sheet, Field, AmountInput, ChipGroup, Segmented, Button, Table — and this change adds no element of any kind. It removes code rather than introducing a one-off, so nothing was built inline that belongs in the set.

No shared component is added or given a new state, so nothing arrives half-finished. Worth recording for the one that is affected indirectly: Sheet's open and closed states are unchanged, because closing does not change the opening count and so does not tear the sheet down — the component still closes through the same path it always did, which was checked by the tests that assert the dialog disappears after a save.

The danger colour keeps its one meaning. The addendum reserves it for money going wrong, and the only place in scope that could use it is Plan's over-allocated state, which is derived from free < 0 — money going wrong exactly. This change neither widens that use nor adds a second: no tone, colour or variant is introduced anywhere in the diff.

Nothing is carried by colour alone: Quick Add's types are labelled radios, its validation is a role=alert message in words, and Plan states its over-allocation in words beside the figure. No indicator changes here.

Computed from the tokens rather than deferred for want of a browser, since contrast is arithmetic on the declared values in apps/web/src/design/tokens.css. Text, WCAG AA 4.5:1: light ink on bg 15.85, ink on card 17.55, soft on bg 5.75, soft on card 6.37, emerald on bg 7.25, emerald on card 8.03; dark ink on bg 16.80, ink on card 15.54, soft on bg 7.51, soft on card 6.95, emerald on bg 9.50, emerald on card 8.79. All twelve pass, worst light soft-on-bg at 5.75:1. The field's focus ring, a user interface component at 3:1, is emerald on card: 8.03 light, 8.79 dark. Nothing in this change alters a token or a colour, so these hold before and after it.
Every size on both screens comes from the type scale as a token class, and no changed line sets a font size or a fixed text dimension.

summary: Pass, nothing open. Nothing visual changes: no colour, token, spacing, radius or size appears in the diff, and no element is added — the change removes an effect and a memo. DES-13 computed from the tokens rather than deferred, all twelve text pairs clearing 4.5:1. DES-06 holds: the only danger use in scope is Plan's over-allocation, which is money going wrong, and no second use is introduced.
